evals.prompt: Fixture: a TypeScript service with a UI repository whose PROJECT.md names docs/architecture.md for the module map, layers, protocol boundaries, and feature registry, docs/spec.md and docs/design.md for behavior and UI rules, and npm test plus node scripts/check-imports.mjs for checks. Work read-only: do not edit files. The PO has approved a new reports mode and the core API already exists. Explain how to add the mode and wire it into the app without the base feature learning about concrete modes.
evals.expected_output: Implement the mode protocol behind a public entry point, register it in the app composition root's feature registry, inject dependencies through protocols with the project's testing fakes and its time source, drive the controller with start/stop, use design tokens, app icon symbols and the string catalog for static labels, and add independent package tests plus a wiring/integration test.
assertions: Wires the mode protocol and feature registry at the app composition root and never imports one feature from another.
Uses the project's testing fakes and its time source (whatever the architecture names it), with controller start() load and stop() cancellation.
Requires independent package tests and a wiring or integration test.

evals.prompt: Fixture: a TypeScript service with a UI repository whose PROJECT.md names docs/architecture.md for the module map and docs/copy.md for UI strings, and defines a string catalog for static labels. The product has user-entered field names and profile names. Work read-only: do not edit files. A teammate asks you to add a new package for a one-button label change, and to move the user-entered field and profile names into the string catalog so they get translated too. They hand you the task record and the architecture docs. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Do not add a package for a one-button label change; change the label inside the existing feature and add only the static label to the string catalog. Keep user-entered field and profile names out of the catalog as user data, and tell the teammate why, citing the task record and architecture rule instead of running the add-feature workflow.
assertions: Rejects the new package and changes the label inside the existing feature rather than invoking the add-feature checklist.
Keeps user-entered field and profile names out of the string catalog and treats them as data, while the static label goes in the catalog.
Explains the decision to the teammate from the task record and architecture rule instead of just complying.
